title: GD&T for machinists: the 14 symbols and when each one matters
summary: A legacy 14-symbol reference with edition awareness and practical inspection questions.

blocks.title: Start with the drawing’s governing edition
blocks.body: The familiar 14-symbol set includes concentricity and symmetry from ASME Y14.5-2009 and earlier practice. ASME Y14.5-2018 removed those two controls. Older drawings still need interpretation under their specified standard; do not silently replace a legacy callout.

blocks.heading: The 14-symbol reading key
blocks.alt: Fourteen labeled geometric characteristic symbols in five groups: form, profile, orientation, location and runout. Concentricity and symmetry are marked legacy.
blocks.caption: Schematic symbol key, not a feature-control-frame specification. Read the named control, its tolerance, modifiers and datums together.

blocks.heading: Form: the feature itself
rows: Straightness
Line element or derived median line, depending on callout
A shaft feature must stay within its stated straightness zone
Flatness
Surface, or a derived median plane where specified
A mounting face must not rock beyond its permitted form error
Circularity
Each circular cross-section
A turned ring can be round yet taper along its length
Cylindricity
The cylindrical surface as a whole
A bearing seat needs a consistent cylindrical form
blocks.caption: Form controls do not reference a datum. Size and applicable envelope requirements still matter.

blocks.heading: Profile: an outline or a complete surface
rows: Profile of a line
Specified line elements of a surface
Inspect a controlled section through a contoured part
Profile of a surface
The specified three-dimensional surface
Inspect a contoured sealing surface
blocks.caption: Datum references and other callout details determine how orientation and location are controlled. “Profile” does not by itself explain the complete requirement.

blocks.heading: Orientation: direction relative to datums
rows: Parallelism
Parallel to the referenced datum
Opposed guide face maintains the stated orientation
Perpendicularity
90° to the referenced datum
Bore axis is square to the locating face
Angularity
Specified basic angle to the datum
An angled fixture face follows the drawing’s basic angle
blocks.caption: Orientation is not a substitute for a location tolerance. Establish the datum reference frame before judging the relation.

blocks.heading: Location and the two legacy controls
rows: Position
Location of a feature, commonly an axis or centre plane
Bolt-pattern holes must assemble relative to the datum system
Concentricity · legacy
Median points relative to a datum axis under the specified legacy rules
A legacy coaxial feature needs the prescribed median-point evaluation
Symmetry · legacy
Median points relative to a datum centre plane under the specified legacy rules
A legacy opposed-feature requirement needs its actual symmetry evaluation
blocks.caption: A dial-indicator sweep is not automatically a valid concentricity measurement. Do not read either legacy control as “looks centred.”

blocks.heading: Runout: surface behavior during rotation about a datum axis
rows: Circular runout
At each specified circular element
Assess variation at a particular ring while rotating
Total runout
Across the controlled surface
Assess the whole journal or face as required
blocks.caption: Runout depends on the datum axis and combines effects; it does not isolate one form error or diagnose its cause.

blocks.heading: Read the whole sentence
blocks.body: A feature-control frame names a characteristic, a tolerance with applicable modifiers, and any datum references in order. Basic dimensions identify theoretically exact geometry. The tolerance zone then says how the real feature may depart. “Position 0.010” without units, zone shape, modifiers or references is not enough to program inspection.

blocks.heading: A datum is the reference; a datum feature is the real part
blocks.body: The labeled face on the workpiece has manufacturing variation. The inspection setup establishes the specified reference from that real feature. Clamping the part on an arbitrary convenient face can change what you measure, even with an accurate indicator or CMM.

blocks.heading: Choose the inspection question
blocks.prompt: A shaft drawing specifies circular runout to datum axis A. What should you ask first?
options: How is datum axis A established in this setup?
Can I use the outside diameter as the datum without checking?
blocks.explanation: The measured variation has meaning only relative to the specified datum axis and controlled elements.

blocks.heading: A useful clarification request
blocks.body: Identify the drawing revision, governing standard, feature and exact callout. Describe the intended inspection setup and what is unclear. Let the responsible designer or quality authority resolve ambiguity; a convenient measurement method does not rewrite the requirement.

items.label: ASME Y14.5: dimensioning and tolerancing
items.detail: Governing standard and edition information; use the edition named on the drawing.

items.label: ASME: legacy concentricity and symmetry chapter
items.detail: Legacy concepts need their actual definitions, not substitution with runout.
